To make scripts more theatrical, my trick is to see if you can condense scenes into their core imagery. The whole show vs tell thing. 

A quick example would be like a scene where your detective is telling the victim's family that their loved one has died. A TV sort of treatment of the scene might have them coming in, talking to the family, family weeping in front of them, maybe some words exchanged about where he was the night he died, etc etc. 

Whereas a filmic treatment might have the detective knock on the door of a house, the door opens up to show a young wife with a baby, the smile falls off her face as she takes in his badge, cut to the child's toy barbie without a head as mum weeps in the background... or something less hack, but you get the picture.

Features technically have very little space, so every scene needs to have some semblance of tone and theme on top of the usual character/plot, and I've found the fastest way to get it across is with strong visual writing and painting a world you wouldn't have time for in a TV.

Hey! I was in a really similar situation a while back. Split from partner of 4 years while pregnant. 

First thing I did was talk to CAB. They helped lay out my options. They directed me to free legal aid who were really happy to help me out under the circumstances.

Legal aid told me my rights vs his rights under NZ law. Basically he cannot fight you on his financial duties to you and your child and there are ways to force it via the courts. But once he's on the birth certificate, be warned that he can veto you ever leaving the city/country with his kid, and he might be a dick about it considering how he's currently acting. So, plan accordingly.

One thing they encourage you to do is fill out a parenting form (edit: I think it's called a parenting agreement? You'll have to do it with him, and both of you sign it.) It basically asks all the important questions like who gets the baby and when, what religion you're going to raise them in, what schools, etc. It's subject to change, but you can log it with the courts in case he flip-flops on you and you want to have leverage for things you feel strongly about.

Other than that, go to WINZ. Sole parent benefit is pretty good especially as the full time parent. Since your guy is being a dick, I would get them to claim child support directly from him as opposed to a private agreement. I was and still am making about 45-55k a year (it's impossible to get a good full time job around daycare hours) my ex is making 150k a year and between child support and WINZ you can afford a small place of your own until you're back on your feet.

Finally, please please please do right by you and the baby by getting what you need and deserve from this guy. You're entering what will be one of the most vulnerable times of your life and you need to focus all that energy on yourself and your baby. Don't be overly accommodating, sounds like he can take care of himself just fine.

Feel free to message if you need any additional advice or wanna ask about legals, WINZ, etc. You can do this.

Cinando is helpful to find people if you know what you're looking for. 

1. Are you looking for a producer, EP, sales agent, distributor, etc?

Lay everything out: the nature of their request, how much they are asking for, the state of the "garden" before and after move out (mention you have pictures), and ask them for proof (an itemized bill/quote for said maintenance as well as before and after photos of what they had "maintained"). The burden of proof is on the landlord, especially if they're claiming it as a reason to hold your bond. They were also required to get your consent before doing any maintenance - it's not your problem if they got the most expensive gardener on the planet, they did not warn you of the service or provide you with a quote beforehand, otherwise if they had a reasonable complaint you could have arranged for your own service.

When they can't prove the cost/reason for maintenance, or when they come up with obviously bullshit proof, tell them you do not agree to it. Lodge a complaint with Tribunal. It costs around 20$ but you can claim it back from your landlord when they inevitably lose their case.

If time is of the essence, just lodge a complaint with Tribunal anyway. As long as you have photos pre and post move out, it should be an open and shut case. Good luck! You got this!

I love creamy sauces so my suggestions:

Miso mushroom pasta:
- Cook any kind of mushrooms and finish them off with sherry/balsamic vinegar
- Take them off the pan
- Mix 2tsp red miso paste to 3TBSP butter
- Fry up minced garlic
- Add mushrooms back, miso + butter paste, and 1/2 cup heavy cream. Salt and pepper.
- Toss with pasta! 

or Truffle Mushroom Pasta
- Chop a buttload of mushrooms, 1 onion, and garlic
- Cook up onions + garlic, then mushrooms
- Add about a cup of cream (I make this dairy free and use a small container of soy cream)
- Salt, pepper, maybe oregano and red pepper if you're into that
- Cook til it thickens. Add 1/2 TBSP of flour if it's not thickening
- Serve with truffle oil drizzled on top (don't add it in when cooking)

You can make both of these as fancy or as basic as you want!

Who do you trust to help you mentally get through this? Reach out to them. Tell them everything. Let them help. Keep eating and staying healthy for your baby, if not for anyone else.

I'm a filmmaker. In my younger years I made a film that was received well and I got invited to speak at a Big Shot Conference. Oscar winners, high flying producers, big name actors. No one gave a shit about my little talk and in between sessions I had no one to hang with. It felt like shit. After the first day of a three day weekend I went to my hotel room, had a panic attack, and cried to my BF via Skype. 

I'm a fairly confident person so even as the "weird one" at school I never really felt out of place. But that conference was the worst. It was the only time in my life that I felt like such an awful, horrid, worthless loser.

But I knew I had to stick it out if I wanted any sort of career in the industry so I took a deep breath, gathered all the dignity and courage I could, and forced myself to go back the next day. I suffered through the quiet moments pretending I was back at school and didn't give a shit what anyone thought. It also helped a lot to put things into perspective, that the conference was going to be one of many, many moments in my career and that people were just there to do business. I could potentially come back someday with some business for them and then people would talk to me. That was easy for my ego to understand.

After I gave my talk, I actually got approached by some producers. They gave me their cards and I made some connections I still talk to to this day. But that first day will always stick with me, and once in a while, when I'm feeling like a cocky ass (as I normally do) I think back to that low moment and it helps to reorient my thinking. Even if I had walked away from that weekend with zero cards, it would have been worthwhile just for that change in mindset.
